title: Fallback
body:
# Fallback

<BurgerAnalogy text={"If the personalized recommendation service fails, our burger restaurant can still show its regular menu rather than block ordering. The standard menu is a fallback: reduced functionality that remains useful and safe. The counter should explain the limitation, and the alternative must preserve important rules such as current prices and allergen information instead of silently substituting unreliable data."} />

An essential strategy for preserving useful functionality during failures by offering an alternative, potentially reduced experience.

## How It Works

Imagine driving to work and finding a traffic jam on your usual route. Instead of waiting indefinitely, you take an alternative route, even if it is slightly longer.

Fallback works similarly in distributed systems: when a service or feature fails, the system switches to a predefined alternative, even if it offers a reduced experience.

## Benefits

<Cards cols={3}>

<Card title="Greater Availability" accent="green">

The system keeps working despite partial failures.

</Card>

<Card title="Better Experience" accent="green">

Users can still access essential features.

</Card>

<Card title="Resilience" accent="green">

The system adapts to adverse conditions.

</Card>

</Cards>

## Real-World Examples

<Cards cols={3}>

<Card title="Local Cache" accent="slate">

When a data service is unavailable, the system uses locally cached data, which may be stale.

</Card>

<Card title="Offline Mode" accent="slate">

Applications let users continue working offline and synchronize once the connection is restored.

</Card>

<Card title="Recommendations" accent="slate">

A recommendation system offers generic suggestions when its personalized service fails.

</Card>

</Cards>

## Best Practices

<Cards cols={3}>

<Card title="Planning" accent="slate">

Identify critical dependencies and prepare fallback strategies in advance.

</Card>

<Card title="Clear Communication" accent="slate">

Tell users when they are using a reduced version of the service.

</Card>

<Card title="Monitoring" accent="slate">

Track fallback usage to identify recurring problems.

</Card>

</Cards>
